general.temas: The general strike and student protests, with demonstrations and clashes in several cities, dominate several front pages. The war in Ukraine and Trump’s statements, artificial intelligence, and the agreement between the EU and the United Kingdom also feature repeatedly. Only Corriere della Sera highlights Toti’s meetings with a businessman and the alleged manipulation of pandemic data in Liguria.
general.motivo_crispacion: Tensions are high over protests against budget policy, rearmament and the cost of living, with clashes between demonstrators and police in several cities. Injured officers, police charges, tear gas and the burning of images of political leaders are mentioned. The war in Ukraine, the allegations concerning Liguria and clashes between parties in the governing majority over tax measures also contribute to the tension. News such as the agreement between the EU and the United Kingdom and sports coverage provides a calmer counterpoint.

Corriere della Sera.resumen:
- The front page highlights investigations in Liguria, with meetings on a yacht and alleged manipulation of pandemic data; the mayor of Genoa calls for clarification.
- A headline questions whether changes to the highway code will reduce casualties.
- The conflict within the governing majority over the Superbonus and the tax on sugary drinks is covered, alongside criticism of borrowing.
- Russia advances toward Kharkiv and Zelensky describes the situation as extremely difficult.
- The paper reports on the complaint against Fedez, who denies being present, and Camila Giorgi’s tax situation; it also offers savings advice.
Corriere della Sera.motivo_populismo: Expressions such as “the case erupts” and “pursued by the tax authorities” dramatize some stories, but there is no apparent appeal to the people against the elites.
Corriere della Sera.sesgo: The selection gives particular prominence to the investigations involving Ligurian authorities and conflicts within the governing majority. Its approach is critical of debt and the effectiveness of the road safety reform.

la Repubblica.resumen:
- Stock markets suffer steep declines, especially in technology and artificial intelligence; another story recounts the experiences of people who have grown wealthy thanks to Anthropic.
- The MPS board considers the price offered by Intesa Sanpaolo fair, but Passera protests and resigns.
- Trump says peace in Ukraine will come soon and highlights his good relations with Putin.
- Thousands of students protest in support of education and against rearmament; a student who stopped masked protesters rejects violence and its exploitation for political purposes.
- Sports coverage highlights Cobolli’s defeat to Alcaraz, the return of V8 engines to Formula 1, and controversies surrounding GTA VI and the campaign against violence toward women.
la Repubblica.motivo_populismo: Expressions such as “black week,” “flight from tech” and “plunge” add drama, although facts predominate and there is no explicit confrontation between the people and the elites.
la Repubblica.sesgo: The selection gives considerable space to finance, sport and student protests, with attention to conflicts and personal experiences. No clear political orientation is apparent across the headlines as a whole.

La Stampa.resumen:
- Trump expects a peace agreement this year; Warsaw reports that two Russian missiles landed in Poland, and there are more casualties in Kyiv.
- The strike against the budget package brings out demonstrators and sees tensions in Turin, Rome and Bologna; effigies of Trump and Netanyahu are burned in Milan.
- China ejects a Bloomberg journalist from a summit after a question about Nvidia; memes about Putin go viral after the Shenzhen meeting.
- The United Kingdom and the EU agree on a temporary stay program for young people, scheduled for 2028.
- An investigation is opened in Paris following a gang rape complaint against Depardieu and Houellebecq; stories about the CEO of Anthropic and Erika Eleniak also feature prominently.
La Stampa.motivo_populismo: Factual reporting predominates, although expressions such as “had dared,” “mystery” and “a flood of memes,” together with the emphasis on clashes, add drama and sensationalism.
La Stampa.sesgo: The selection favors international conflicts and tensions at the protests, although it also includes a student’s appeal against violence. Some stories focus on spectacle and curiosity, with no apparent systematic appeal to the people against the elites.

Il Giornale.resumen:
- L’Aquila celebrates an inauguration after 17 years; Meloni highlights the funding provided.
- Trump talks about Iran and Ukraine, while Melania criticizes White House flatterers.
- The general strike leads to tensions and leaves seven officers injured; protests in Rome and Bologna are also highlighted.
- The front page includes political reactions concerning Berlusconi and Elvis Demce’s attempted suicide in prison.
- Several headlines address Islam, immigration and the veil; others question proposals concerning cannabis, condoms and an inclusive Christmas.
Il Giornale.motivo_populismo: Expressions such as “shock amendments,” “the burka that blinds the left” and “massacre narrowly averted” resort to alarmism, disparagement and simplification.
Il Giornale.sesgo: A critical approach to the left, Islam and inclusive initiatives is apparent in the selection of stories and language highlighting conflicts and risks. The front page also reproduces statements favorable to Meloni’s handling of affairs and to Berlusconi.

Il Fatto Quotidiano.resumen:
- Student protests and the general strike bring together young people, teachers and workers in several Italian cities.
- In Milan, demonstrations continue into the night and a group occupies the former slaughterhouse.
- In Turin, police use baton charges, water cannon and tear gas against demonstrators.
- A court orders the reopening of the account of a collective sanctioned by the United States; judicial developments in two homicide cases also feature prominently.
- International coverage includes protests in Brussels, agreements between the EU and the United Kingdom, and conflicting accusations concerning Iran.
Il Fatto Quotidiano.motivo_populismo: Informative headlines predominate, but some quotes use emotive and confrontational language, such as “broken dreams” and “no one represents us,” and the word “alarm” appears in relation to Iran.
Il Fatto Quotidiano.sesgo: The front page gives extensive prominence to the protests and the voices of students and demonstrators, paying particular attention to their demands and police conduct. The selection gives less space to other perspectives on the demonstrations.

opiniones.comunista:
Today I see an alliance on the streets that deserves attention: workers, students and teachers are protesting against the high cost of living, the lack of investment in education and rearmament. To me, these are not separate demands. They reveal a struggle over which needs receive the resources we all produce together.

While stock markets suffer a week of steep losses, we are being urged to entrust the future to individual savings and the markets. I argue for the opposite: strong public education and pension systems, funded fairly, and collective ownership of strategic sectors, under the democratic control of workers and society. It is not enough to spread the losses when speculation fails while leaving the profits in private hands.

The protest must be peaceful: its strength lies in organizing the majority, not in violence.
opiniones.anarquista:
I see the strike and the marches by students and teachers as a necessary response to the lack of investment in education and the arms race. It is not enough to ask parties to administer our lives better: those who study and work should be able to decide directly on their needs, through assemblies and self-managed organizations, without permanent bosses or blindly delegating authority.

In Turin, police responded to demonstrators with water cannon and tear gas. That way of managing protest shows why I distrust a state that reserves control of the streets for itself. I also reject violence at demonstrations: it weakens the freedom we claim to defend. Mutual aid and collective action do not need to impose obedience; they can build a force capable of sustaining both individual autonomy and shared freedom.
opiniones.liberal:
I see a legitimate concern for the future in the student protests. But I do not believe the answer is to hand more resources and powers to a state that already asks too much of those who work and run businesses. Better education also needs freedom of choice, a diversity of approaches and responsibility in the use of public money. Defending the right to protest also requires respecting the freedom of those who need to move around and rejecting violence.

The dispute over the Superbonus and the drinks tax is a reminder of another principle: tax rules must be predictable. I oppose retroactive measures and new taxes that reduce the ability of families and businesses to make their own decisions. I prefer low taxes, restrained spending and open markets: lasting prosperity comes from free people who take risks and take responsibility for their decisions, not from privileges handed out by those in power.
opiniones.extrema_derecha:
Today I see an Italy that needs to regain control of its destiny. The protests by students and workers deserve to be heard, but throwing bottles and firecrackers at police is not exercising a right: it is endangering our ability to live together. Safety on the streets must be a priority, not a negotiable concession.

I also believe the expulsion of the aspiring jihadist is a reminder of why we need guarded borders, rigorous checks and sovereign decisions about who may remain in our country. That does not mean judging entire communities, but demanding compliance with our laws. And while elites debate agreements and the international balance of power, I want a nation capable of defending its interests, its traditions and the future of its young people. Peace in Ukraine matters, but Italy must not give up its right to decide for itself.
opiniones.centro:
I see in the protests by students and workers a demand that politicians should not dismiss as noise: invest in education and offer prospects for the future. Listening to them requires negotiating priorities and funding commitments responsibly, not promising everything without explaining who will pay. It also requires distinguishing peaceful protest from episodes of violence, which do not strengthen any cause.

Meanwhile, the attacks on Ukraine are a reminder that wishing for peace is not enough. I support sustained diplomacy, but a lasting peace requires listening to Kyiv and protecting its security. And I welcome the agreement between the European Union and the United Kingdom on youth mobility: it does not resolve all the differences over Brexit, but it shows that dialogue and gradual progress can restore tangible opportunities to people.
